To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the satisfiability problem of all decidable and tractably decidable hybrid logics is in NP, and that the satisfiability problems of all tractably decidable logics can be decided in polynomial time by an algorithm that is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of downarrow binders.
the satisfiability problems of hybrid logics without the downarrow binder are decidable.
the satisfiability problem is decidable for hybrid logics that do not allow the downarrow binder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects of this problem: the complexity of the satisfiability problem and the expressive power of the logic.
the following questions: (1) which fragments of hybrid logic are decidable? (2) which fragments of the logic are tractable?

the following questions: What is the complexity of satisfiability for fragments of hybrid logic? What are the computational consequences of restricting the use of the binder? What is the complexity if we allow the downarrow binder but restrict the use of nominals?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no decidable fragments of full hybrid logic, but there are many tractable fragments.
satisfiability for hybrid logic is undecidable, unless the logic is very restricted.

the satisfiability problem of the fragment of hybrid logics without the downarrow binder (i.e., with only the standard modal and the nominals) is decidable in 2EXPTIME, while for the fragment with the downarrow operator it is undecidable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the satisfiability problem is undecidable for the fragment of hybrid logics containing the downarrow binder and a single propositional variable, and is decidable for the fragment without the downarrow binder.
the satisfiability problem of the logic is undecidable for the downarrow binder and decidable for the uparrow binder, and for the downarrow with the uparrow binder.
we have found many decidable and tractably satisfiable hybrid logics, but also that the complexity landscape is quite complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of hybrid logic depends crucially on the interaction between the modal and the first-order operators.
the satisfiability problem of a hybrid logic is decidable if and only if its modal base logic has the finite model property.

, in order to obtain decidability, one needs to impose restrictions on the modal depth of formulas, the nesting of the downarrow binder, and on the nesting of propositional variables in the scope of the downarrow.
